newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan agency to seek charges against nuclear firm.
newsitem.headline: Japan agency to seek charges against nuclear firm.

text.p: Japan's Science and Technology Agency is to ask prosecutors to file charges against operators of a nuclear fuel reprocessing plant who admitted a cover-up of the nation's worst nuclear accident.
Agency officials said on Tuesday they will file a complaint with prosecutors as early as Wednesday against the state-run Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC).

The complaint, the first step in a legal process to bring formal charges against a person or institution, stems from the cover-up of an explosion at the PNC's nuclear waste processing plant which exposed 37 workers to low levels of radiation.
The explosion, on March 11, occurred at a bituminisation facility at a PNC complex housing Japan's only nuclear fuel reprocessing plant in Tokaimura, just 160 km (100 miles) northeast of Tokyo.
Low-level nuclear waste is mixed with asphalt at the facility to be placed in drums for permanent storage.

Officials of PNC admitted last week that it had falsified a formal report on the explosion. Science and Technology Agency officials said the falsified report may have violated Japan's Nuclear Reactor Control Law.

Asked about the rare move by a government agency to file a legal complaint against a state-run corporation, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto told reporters on Tuesday: "What do you mean by rare? It's rare enough to lie about things like this."
